blockers.title_at_research: A whole class of task cannot be completed by any runner in this repo
blockers.blocked_on_at_research: Several open tasks fix the /whattask GENERATOR, which lives at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/mit-claude-setup/mit-setup/1.9.5/commands/whattask.md` -- OUTSIDE this repo. No `touches` a plan for this repo can grant will ever reach it, so `/runtask` can only ever record `partial` on them, however many times they are attempted (one already has). This is the same shape as tasks whose fix is a `whattask.json` rewrite, one level further out. HOW DO YOU WANT THESE HANDLED? Options: (a) work the plugin repo directly in a separate session and keep these out of this plan; (b) let this plan grant absolute plugin paths, accepting that they are outside the repo the locks protect; (c) mark them explicitly unrunnable so a runner skips them rather than burning a cycle. At least three current tasks are affected: the touches-exists check, the `creates:` mode, and the test-file rule.

blockers.title_at_research: Powerplay's regrid refusal rests on a naming artefact
blockers.blocked_on_at_research: BOTH AXES ARE NOW MEASURED, at 7bcd3fe, and the question is a clean yes/no. Powerplay refuses --regrid in presets.json. The refusal rests on melody falling 0.9930 -> 0.9643 under regrid (2.88pp). SEQUENCE AXIS (difflib, what fidelity.naming_split ships): repairing NAMES alone recovers 2.71pp of that 2.88pp -- a naming share of 94% on just 7 renames, and all 7 are -1 semitone (A#4/A-4 x3, D-5/C#5 x2, G-5/F#5 x2). So on this reading almost the whole 'loss' is siddump naming the same note differently, not different music. THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION WAS TESTED AND FAILS: difflib chooses the pairing, so the count is alignment-dependent (its own docstring says so). Re-measured on the FRAME axis -- substituting only where both arms strike on the SAME frame -- it makes 36 renames spanning -12..+13 semitones and leaves melody at 0.9531, BELOW the unrepaired 0.9643, for a share of -39%. That is a worse alignment, not a truer one: it pairs notes that merely coincide in time, which after a regrid are different notes. So the 94% stands on measurement rather than on the absence of an alternative. WHAT REGRID BUYS, and it is the other half of the trade: --regrid exists to remove integrated drift, which NO FIDELITY.MD COLUMN CAN SEE -- a tune playing the right music 0.78% fast forever scores perfectly. Adopting it means accepting a melody number that is 2.88pp lower on paper for a timing gain the report cannot show you. THE QUESTION: adopt --regrid for Powerplay on the strength of the 94% naming share, or keep the refusal? A listen would settle it independently and none has been taken.

Repairing NAMES alone recovers 2.71pp -- a 94% naming share on 7 renames, all -1 semitone; the frame-axis alternative was tested and is WORSE (0.9531), so the 94% stands on measurement. THE DIRECTLY ANALOGOUS CASE REVERSED: One_on_One was refused for the same reason with a recorded -37.0pp collapse, and at 180 s its melody IMPROVES 0.9903 -> 0.9952; it was adopted at v0.5.459.
